name: Cal.diy
tagline: A scheduling platform for bookings, availability, calendars, and integrations.
hook: Limits code PRs to 500 changed lines and ten files, then demonstrates how to split booking and calendar features.
summary: Cal.diy uses short do-and-don't lists, code examples, and firm pull-request size limits. It also covers security-sensitive field selection, one exception to direct imports, and larger workflows that need explicit approval.

techniques.title: Make a size limit measurable and scoped
techniques.body: The guide counts additions plus deletions and code files, while excluding documentation, lockfiles, and generated artifacts. It then offers layer, feature, preparatory-refactor, and dependency-order splits.
techniques.quote:
- **Lines changed**: Keep PRs under 500 lines of code (additions + deletions)
- **Files changed**: Keep PRs under 10 code files
- **Single responsibility**: Each PR should do one thing well

techniques.title: Connect field selection to sensitive-data exposure
techniques.body: Prisma examples contrast explicit select fields with include fetching an entire related record. The prohibitions separately name credential.key as a field that must never be exposed.

techniques.title: State the local exception to a repository-wide import rule
techniques.body: The root favors direct source imports, but API v2 lacks path mappings for two packages. Its section requires re-exporting through platform-libraries and shows both steps and the failing direct import.
techniques.quote: When importing from `@calcom/features` or `@calcom/trpc` into `apps/api/v2`, **do not import directly** because the API v2 app's `tsconfig.json` doesn't have path mappings for these modules, which causes "module not found" errors.

techniques.title: Keep a larger planning workflow opt-in
techniques.body: Spec-driven development is offered for complex features, but its presence does not make it mandatory. The guide names the explicit user trigger and points to the separate workflow document.
techniques.quote: For complex features, you can use spec-driven development when explicitly requested.

steal: Define what counts toward a PR-size limit and show decomposition examples.
Explain which broad data-fetching patterns can expose sensitive fields.
Put package-specific exceptions beside the general rule they refine.
Make optional workflows conditional on an explicit trigger.
